question: May text a bank types for its own agents reach a model? D-07 lets only the Ask question (and, since PRD 0.5, an agent-access description) reach a model. D-32 says tenant text never reaches the tenant runner, and asks for confirmation with D-07 before chunk 11. Two features involve text a bank writes: AGT-05's 'research a topic', and a D-89 scope item's name, official reference and source addresses.
recommended_default: Yes, as a second named exception beside Ask. The text is limited to length-capped structured fields plus jurisdiction and regime keys. It is screened as untrusted and sent only through the logged wrapper to an approved EU endpoint. The bank's AI switch and budget cap stop it, it is never logged, and it never reaches a platform run. An ADR records the exception. Until you answer, c11-research-requests, d89-researcher-definition and d89-agent-research build and ship a keys-only path. The free-text path is a small follow-on that is not in this plan.
answer: Alex, 2026-09-25: yes, guarded, as the default says (D-98).

question: D-89 says the bank's agents fill its 'regulation and control inventories'. What is a control inventory in data terms?
recommended_default: A control is a REG-05 linked internal item of the control kind. The agent proposes it against the private obligation it serves, and the same private approval creates it, so no new table is needed. If you meant a standard's controls (REG-08 units), say so. REG-08 keeps everything under a standard away from models. If this is unanswered at R2 close, OWN-05 is named as held.
answer: Alex, 2026-09-25: a REG-05 internal item of the control kind, as the default says (D-99).

question: Who decides a re-tag batch (PRO-04)? Today's four-eyes check compares only the proposer and the reviewer. With no editor staffed (D-62), an agent may approve only kinds whose record names its confirming agent, and obligation_term does not. As built now, a batch waits for a person.

question: Which source may ID-07's committed authenticator allow-list be built from? ADR 0048 says the FIDO Metadata Service. Its relying-party terms (Verification_Log row 47) forbid copying, displaying or deriving from MDS data without a written agreement, and this list is committed and shown to banks.
recommended_default: Build it by hand from vendors' own published attestation roots (for example Yubico's), with model names we write and no MDS data. Sign FIDO's agreement only if a bank needs a model whose vendor publishes no roots. Until then the list is absent, and a device-bound policy is refused with empty_authenticator_list.
answer: Alex, 2026-09-25: skip it in R2. The device-bound policy (ID-07, ID-S16, ID-S29) moves out of R2; banks can still require passkeys, not specific models (D-100).

question: D-89 put a bank's own regulations in R2 and handed their PRD text to the R2 plan. r2-spec-d89 writes it as PRD 0.7's OWN group, recorded as D-91 and answered by default.
